name: RAP: Retrieval-Augmented Planning with Contextual Memory for Multimodal LLM Agents

task_domain: Embodied / decision-making and web interaction for LLM agents. Spans text-based embodied household tasks (ALFWorld), web navigation / online shopping (WebShop), and multimodal robotic manipulation (Franka Kitchen, Meta-World). General retrieval-augmented planning framework for sequential decision-making in both text-only and multimodal embodied environments.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent, closed-loop sequential decision-making over a finite horizon of H timesteps. A frozen LLM/VLM acts as the agent (no gradient training of the policy); the only learning is offline construction of an episodic memory of past SUCCESSFUL task executions. At each timestep the agent forms an action plan, picks an action, and receives an observation (textual world-state for ALFWorld/WebShop; fixed-viewpoint camera images for Franka Kitchen/Meta-World). RAP augments the standard ReAct loop with four modules (Memory, Reasoner, Retriever, Executor): the Reasoner generates overall plan, action plans, and retrieval keys; the Retriever selects the most relevant memory logs by a weighted similarity score; the Executor consumes the retrieved past experiences via in-context learning to choose the next action. Supervision is the bank of self-collected successful trajectories (no labeled retrieval data; off-the-shelf embedders). For multimodal benchmarks, a small MLP policy network trained on 25 D4RL expert demonstrations per task maps high-level VLM plans to low-level control actions. Evaluation runs recursively for up to 3 trials (d_max=3), with memory growing from successes in earlier trials (and optionally a 1000-task training set in RAP_train).
what_is_retrieved: Past experiences = episodic logs of prior SUCCESSFUL task executions. Each log L_i stores the task information T_i, the overall plan p_i, and the full trajectory tau (sequences of action plans, actions, and observations). Retrieved units are windows of these trajectories (action-observation sub-trajectories) centered on the most similar action; for multimodal tasks the observations are stored images.
retrieval_grounding: GROWING / episodic memory the agent writes. The retrievable store is a memory database of the agent's own past successful trajectories, built offline from prior attempts/training tasks and grown across recursive trials. It is not a static external knowledge corpus (no Wikipedia/KB/API docs); retrieval targets self-generated experience.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k similarity retrieval (no completeness or precision-driven variable-size objective). A constant number of experiences and a fixed window of actions are extracted per retrieval, e.g. ALFWorld action-based: 4 experiences x 10 actions before/after the most similar action; observation-based: 8 experiences x 5 actions; WebShop: 3 experiences x 5 actions. There is no notion of recovering a complete minimal set; k and window sizes are fixed hyperparameters tuned per environment.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Retrieve: yes (similarity-based retrieval of past cases). Reuse: yes (in-context analogy-making / ICL adaptation by the Executor, incl. WebShop intra-task 'A:B::C:D' analogy). Revise: no (no execution-feedback revision of a retrieved case; the LLM adapts implicitly but there is no explicit case-revision step). Retain: partial (new SUCCESSFUL trajectories are written back to memory across recursive trials / training, so [Retrieve, Reuse, partial-Retain]; Revise not implemented).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper frames itself as Retrieval-Augmented Planning / memory-augmented RAG for LLM agents and emphasizes LLM 'analogy-making'; it does NOT cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner and does not call itself case-based reasoning, though it realizes CBR-like Retrieve/Reuse/Retain mechanisms under the RAG-with-memory framing.
retrieval_unit: Sub-trajectory: a window of an action-observation trajectory centered on the most similar action (rather than the full trajectory, to reduce noise). The stored case is a full episodic log (task + overall plan + trajectory), but at retrieval time only a centered action/observation window from each of k experiences is injected. For multimodal tasks the unit includes the visual observation(s) of the windowed sub-trajectory.
index_source: Growing episodic memory induced from the agent's own runs. Built offline by having agents attempt tasks and saving streams of successful episodes; expanded online across recursive trials (successes from earlier trials and, in RAP_train, 1000 training-set tasks are added). Test-time / deployment growth across trials; not a static offline-frozen corpus.
index_structure_topology: Flat similarity store with metadata/context keys: logs are embedded (sentence-transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2 for text; CLIP ViT-B/32 for images) and retrieved by cosine similarity. Keyed by task information, overall plan, and a Reasoner-generated retrieval key; in constrained-task environments (e.g. Franka Kitchen with 5 tasks) retrieval is filtered to same task type, and WebShop adds product-category keying. No graph or hierarchical index; effectively a flat vector index with adaptive, context-keyed weighting.
retriever_type: Dense (off-the-shelf embedding similarity). Cosine similarity over frozen sentence-transformer (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) text embeddings and CLIP-based ViT image embeddings; a hand-designed weighted average of task, overall-plan, and retrieval-key similarities. No BM25, no learned/generative retriever; an LLM (Reasoner) only constructs the retrieval key, not the matching function.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf, no training). The retriever uses fixed pretrained embedders (sentence-transformers, CLIP) with cosine similarity; component weights (w_t, w_p, w_k) and which similarity equation to use (observation-based vs action-based) are hand-set/adaptive heuristics per environment, not learned. There is no contrastive training, LM-feedback, preference, or RL signal optimizing the retriever.
query_construction: Two-level, Reasoner-generated. (1) At task start the overall plan is generated from the task and used (with task info) as the query. (2) During the loop, whenever the Reasoner emits an action plan, it derives a concise retrieval key from it (e.g. action plan 'I need to find the watch' -> retrieval key 'search watch'; 'put' -> 'action put'). The key is matched against logged observations (search/locate) or logged actions (interact), and in multimodal settings the key corresponds to the current visual observation.
query_granularity: Both task-level and step/state-level (two-level retrieval). An initial task-level retrieval at t=0 using task + overall plan, then step-level re-retrieval each time the Reasoner produces a new action plan and corresponding retrieval key during the trajectory.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / agent-initiated. Retrieval happens once at task start, then again at every step where the Reasoner generates an action plan (which triggers a new retrieval-key-based query). Per Algorithm 1, retrieval is re-invoked inside the while-loop whenever an action plan (vs. a directly-executable action) is produced.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Agent-initiated by plan type: a re-retrieval is triggered whenever the Reasoner outputs an 'action plan' (rather than a directly executable environment action), at which point a retrieval key is generated and the Retriever is called again. No token-confidence, attention-uncertainty, or learned-complexity-classifier trigger; the schedule is determined by the ReAct-style think/act branching in the Reasoner.
reranking: None. A single weighted-similarity scoring step selects the top experiences; there is no second-stage reranker (no cross-encoder, RRF, or instruction-tuned reranking). The only refinement is selecting a centered trajectory window from each retrieved log.
retrieved_context_refinement: Windowing / truncation: for each retrieved experience only a window of the trajectory centered around the most similar action is passed to the agent (e.g. 10 or 5 actions before/after), explicitly to avoid the noise of full trajectories. No learned distillation, decompose-recompose, distractor classifier, or compression model.
tool_document_engineering: N/A. RAP retrieves past experience trajectories, not tool/API documents; no docstring processing, synthetic-query augmentation, or tool-embedding tuning.
index_content_separation: Partial / implicit: lightweight embedded keys (task, overall plan, retrieval key embeddings) are matched first, then only a centered window of the heavier full trajectory log is loaded into the prompt on demand. This is not framed as a formal progressive-disclosure / SOP-index-then-content design, but functions as index-then-windowed-content.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A. No tool index or integration protocol (no RapidAPI/RESTful/MCP/function-calling registry); the 'store' is an experience memory, grown across trials but not a live-synchronized tool catalog with CRUD.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A. No inter-tool dependency modeling. (The closest analogue is WebShop intra-task relationship reasoning between a task's scenario and its actions, but this concerns task-action correspondence, not tool dependencies.)
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation via in-context learning (case reuse). The Executor (an LLM/VLM) receives the retrieved past-experience windows together with the task, overall plan, and current trajectory, and generates the next action by analogy-making/ICL, mirroring how humans reuse past experience. No weight updates, no latent-token injection; retrieved trajectories are injected as in-context exemplars.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved retrieve-then-act within a closed loop, on top of ReAct. The Reasoner first produces an overall plan and an initial retrieval; then in the loop the Executor generates either an action (executed in the environment) or an action plan; an action plan triggers retrieval-key generation and re-retrieval of relevant experiences, which then condition the next Executor action. Retrieval is woven step-by-step into planning/acting (no MCTS/tree search, no single plan-then-retrieve phase).
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-step / per-action-plan within a rollout: retrieval is interleaved at the granularity of each Reasoner-generated action plan (think step) inside the ReAct-style think-act loop, i.e. roughly per-reasoning-step, not per-token and not only per-final-answer.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM-prompted in-context adaptation (verbatim-window ICL exemplars + analogy). Retrieved trajectory windows are presented as exemplars and the Executor LLM adapts them to the current situation by analogy-making; WebShop additionally uses an explicit intra-task analogy ('A is to B as C is to D') relating each memory action to its scenario to project onto the current scenario. No execution-feedback-driven case revision, critic, or RL-reuse finetuning.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw trajectory windows (action-observation text, and stored images for multimodal tasks) injected as in-context exemplars. Not distilled into strategies/guidelines, not converted to executable programs, not latent/soft tokens. The agent draws implicitly from raw experiences without an extra insight-extraction step (contrasted with ExpeL).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw trajectory (low abstraction): windows of action-observation sequences from past successful episodes, deliberately kept as raw experience rather than distilled insights, strategies, or reusable workflows. The paper relies on the LLM's analogy-making over raw patterns rather than on abstracted rules.
noise_robustness_mechanism: (1) Trajectory windowing: only a window centered on the most similar action is passed, explicitly to reduce noise from full trajectories. (2) Memory contains only SUCCESSFUL executions, so retrieved exemplars are prototypical/correct. (3) Adaptive similarity routing: switching between observation-based and action-based similarity (and constrained-task / category filtering) to retrieve more contextually relevant logs. No retriever-aware training, learned relevance evaluator, or self-reflection over retrieved content.
memory_type: Episodic (experience memory of past successful task trajectories), text and multimodal (images stored for embodied tasks).
write_back: True. The system stores new successful task executions into the memory database: initial logs are collected by attempting tasks and saving successful episodes, and the database is expanded with successes from subsequent recursive trials (and, in RAP_train, from the 1000-task training set).
online_growth: Yes (across trials at evaluation/deployment). The memory grows over recursive trials (d_max up to 3): successful tasks from preceding trials are added to memory for later trials. It is not frozen after a single offline induction. (Within a single trial the store is fixed; growth occurs between trials.)
write_back_trigger: On-success only. A trajectory is written to memory only when the task is solved successfully (e.g. in WebShop, tasks with reward = 1 are counted as successful and added). Failed trajectories are not stored; there is no per-step or reflective write of failures.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only. Only successful executions are stored and retrieved; failed/negative experiences are not added to memory (contrasting with Reflexion which reflects on failures within a task). RAP avoids past failures indirectly by retrieving prototypical successful executions, not by storing failure cases.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only. New successful trajectories are appended to the memory database across trials; existing stored entries are not mutated, merged, refined, or pruned (no dedup/forget/link-and-evolve described).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval is fixed similarity top-k with hand-set adaptive weights and routing rules; it is not an RL/value-based or otherwise learned selection policy. The LLM Reasoner only constructs the retrieval key; the matching/selection is deterministic cosine-similarity ranking.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Cross-model memory transfer (a form of sharing). Because experiences are model-independent, memory built with one model can be reused by another: the paper shows memory constructed with GPT-3.5 improves a Llama2-13b agent (and GPT-3.5 itself) in a transfer-learning ablation. This is cross-model sharing of a single shared memory store, not concurrent multi-agent collective memory.
benchmarks: ALFWorld (134 unseen games, six task types: Pick/Clean/Heat/Cool/Look/Pick2), WebShop (1.18M Amazon products; 100 evaluation instructions), Franka Kitchen (5 selected tasks: cabinet, microwave, burner, light, kettle), Meta-World (5 selected tasks: assemble, button, drawer, hammer, bin). LLMs/VLMs: GPT-3.5 (gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct), GPT-4 (gpt-4-0613), Llama2-13b-chat for text; LLaVA-v1.5-13B and CogVLM-17B for multimodal. Embedders: sentence-transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (text), CLIP ViT-B/32 (images).
benchmark_family: Embodied (ALFWorld; and robotic-manipulation Franka Kitchen / Meta-World) + web (WebShop). Multimodal embodied robotics (Franka Kitchen, Meta-World) plus text-based embodied (ALFWorld) and web-navigation (WebShop).
baselines: Act, ReAct (Yao et al. 2023), Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023), ADaPT (Prasad et al. 2023) on textual benchmarks (ALFWorld, WebShop). For multimodal benchmarks, the base VLMs without RAP (LLaVA, CogVLM) serve as the baselines (LLaVA vs LLaVA+RAP; CogVLM vs CogVLM+RAP). RAP is also compared across base models (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Llama2-13b) vs ReAct.
key_metrics: Task success rate (%) for ALFWorld (per task type and overall), Franka Kitchen, and Meta-World; for WebShop both Success Rate (%) and average reward/overall Score (%). Reported per base model and across trials.
headline_result: RAP improves over ReAct by 33.6% (ALFWorld), 13.0% (WebShop), 18.2% (Franka Kitchen), and 12.7% (Meta-World). On ALFWorld with GPT-3.5, RAP reaches 85.8% overall success vs ReAct 52.2%, Reflexion 74.6%, ADaPT 71.6%; RAP_train (memory from 1000 training tasks) reaches 91.0%; RAP with GPT-4 reaches 94.8%. RAP with GPT-3.5 matches ReAct with GPT-4 (85.8%) and RAP_train (GPT-3.5) surpasses ReAct-GPT-4. The paper claims SOTA in textual scenarios.
ablations: (1) Retriever-type on ALFWorld (GPT-3.5, d_max=3): RAP_act (action-only) 82.1%, RAP_obs (observation-only) 84.3%, full adaptive RAP 85.8%, and RAP_clip (using CLIP image observations instead of text) 86.6% (slightly best), showing direct image retrieval can beat text-converted observations and that adaptively switching action/observation info helps. (2) WebShop retriever components on Llama2-13b: ReAct 31.0% / 64.6 score -> RAP_act 33.0/68.6 -> RAP_obs 33.0/69.0 -> RAP_intra (intra-task analogy) 34.0/69.3 -> RAP_cat (product-category retrieval) 35.0/69.9 -> full RAP 36.0/71.1 (overall +5.0% success, +6.5 score on Llama2; +13.0% success, +14.3 score on GPT-3.5). (3) Transfer learning (ALFWorld, d_max=1): GPT-3.5 44.0% -> 63.4% with GPT-3.5-built memory; Llama2-13b 20.9% -> 27.6% with GPT-3.5-built memory, showing model-independent memory transfer. (4) Multimodal: LLaVA 43.4 Franka / 65.4 MetaWorld -> +RAP 61.6 / 79.2; CogVLM 44.2 / 61.5 -> +RAP 56.9 / 68.8.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics (success rate, score) are reported; there are no separate intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k, nDCG, retrieval precision). Retriever quality is assessed only indirectly via end-task success in the retriever ablations.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome-based (final task success rate / reward score). Process quality is examined only qualitatively via example ReAct-vs-RAP trajectories in the appendix (showing RAP reaches success in fewer / correct steps where ReAct fails); no quantitative step-wise or trajectory-quality metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency is addressed mainly via a fixed, small injected context (constant number of experiences and a fixed trajectory window) to bound prompt size and avoid noise; and by showing RAP-GPT-3.5 matching/surpassing ReAct-GPT-4 (cheaper model reaching a stronger model's performance via memory). Max steps are capped (ALFWorld 50, WebShop 15) and trials at d_max=3. No explicit token-count, dollar-cost, latency, or number-of-retrieval-calls measurements are reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k, budget-capped by windowing. ALFWorld: action-based retrieval extracts 4 experiences with 10 actions before/after the most similar action; observation-based extracts 8 experiences with 5 actions before/after. WebShop: 3 experiences with 5 actions before/after. A constant number of current-trajectory steps is also kept. k and window sizes are fixed hyperparameters per environment (not adaptive/precision-driven); only same-task-type or category filtering narrows the candidate pool in constrained environments.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark-construction paper; evaluates on existing benchmarks ALFWorld, WebShop, Franka Kitchen, Meta-World).
builds_on: ReAct (Yao et al. 2023) — RAP explicitly extends the ReAct reason-act loop with memory retrieval; Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Lewis et al. 2020) for the retrieve-then-generate paradigm; Chain-of-Thought (Wei et al. 2022) for reasoning; the 'LLMs as general pattern machines' analogy-making idea (Mirchandani et al. 2023); sentence-transformers/Sentence-BERT (Reimers & Gurevych 2019) and CLIP (Radford et al. 2021) as off-the-shelf retrievers; VLM foundations LLaVA (Liu et al. 2023) and CogVLM (Wang et al. 2023c); D4RL demonstrations and policy-network mapping for embodied control.
contrasts_with: Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023) — reflects on FAILED trajectories within a task, insights restricted to that task; ADaPT (Prasad et al. 2023) — decomposes into sub-tasks and re-executes but still reflects only within-task; ExpeL (Zhao et al. 2023) — passes all generated experiences to the LLM to explicitly extract text-based insights. RAP instead implicitly draws from a diverse range of successful experiences across tasks via similarity retrieval + in-context analogy, without an extra insight-extraction step, and extends from textual to multimodal contexts (a first for memory-retrieval multimodal agents per the authors).
lineage: Sub-topic B/F lineage of memory-/experience-augmented LLM-agent planning (RAG-with-memory for agentic decision-making). Sits in the ReAct -> Reflexion/ExpeL line of experiential agents, distinguished by cross-task similarity retrieval of raw successful trajectories and by pioneering multimodal (VLM) experience retrieval for embodied robotics tasks.
